methodology: Current view derived from append-only reviewed permit observations in R2 plus automated operational evidence from SGO and Waymo S2. Official permit/status source pages are monitored for changes; prior observations remain in history.

states_status_notes.note: Florida law (2019) opened the door to AV operation and FLHSMV has titling/registration procedures for AVs, but it's unclear whether there's a distinct AV-specific permit beyond standard vehicle registration, and no public roster was found; FLHSMV's own guidance suggests company-level detail would require a public records request.

Georgia has ADS-specific statute and real Waymo/other operations (confirmed via this Observatory's SGO and Waymo S2 data), but no state permit roster was found -- unclear whether Georgia operates a permit regime at all versus general statutory authorization.

Nevada DMV requires an Autonomous Vehicle Testing Registry application (form OBL-326) and a separate Autonomous Vehicle Certification Registry for operation (form OBL-326A) -- a real permit regime with real applicants -- but no public roster of current holders was found; would require a direct records request to DMV.
Ohio requires registration with DriveOhio (created/reauthorized by executive order) before testing AVs on public roads, but no public roster of registrants was found.

Senate Bill 2807 (89th Legislature, 2025) created a MANDATORY TxDMV authorization for commercial automated-vehicle operation in Texas, enforceable since May 28, 2026 (90 days after final implementing rules took effect Feb 27, 2026). TxDMV can issue/revoke authorizations and provides a law-enforcement-only tool to verify a vehicle's authorization status, but publishes no public roster of authorization holders. This corrects an earlier, now-outdated assessment that Texas had no AV-specific permit regime -- it does, as of 2026, and it is actively enforced.
